result.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
result.summary: Despite advances in automated liver lesion segmentation, a gap remains between image-derived predictions and clinically interpretable radiology reports. Bridging this gap requires quantitative measurements that are both reproducible and traceable. We present an evidence-grounded agentic AI framework that connects liver and lesion segmentation with deterministic quantification and structured reporting. TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models delineate the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions, while computational tools extract volumes, dimensions, counts, and anatomical locations. A large language model (LLM) organizes these measurements into a predefined reporting schema, with numerical consistency checks against source measurements. On 51 LiTS cases, the segmentation stage achieved a liver Dice score of 0.947, lesion sensitivity of 75.6%, and positive predictive value of 68.9%. Exploratory screening of 25,494 MERLIN reports identified 10,208 (40.0%) with liver-related abnormalities. By connecting quantitative imaging evidence with agentic report generation, this work takes a step toward human-centered medical AI that prioritizes traceability and clinical relevance.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建肝脏及病灶分割、确定性量化与 LLM 结构化报告生成的临床流水线，并在 LiTS、MERLIN 数据上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于医学影像分割与报告生成的应用型 pipeline，分割输出直接交给 LLM 按模板填写并做数值一致性检查，不涉及推理期视觉状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
